deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's survey, preparing his Nov.-Dec. 1967 IHES lectures on crystals, of Washnitzer-Monsky (W.M.) cohomology.

The previous page sets things up. For a smooth affine k-algebra A_0 (k perfect of characteristic p, W = W(k), K = Frac W), W.M. take a weakly complete (dagger) lift A of A_0 over W. They show that a map u_0: A_0 -> A'_0 lifts, and that the induced map on H^*(Omega^._{A/W}) depends only on u_0. Hence H^*(Omega^._{A/W}) is a canonical invariant of A_0. Grothendieck notes two restrictions: this is proved only for 'special' A_0 (of which there are enough), and in their notes only after tensoring with K. Gluing these invariants gives cohomology sheaves H^*_{X_0} of W-modules on a smooth X_0, but not yet global invariants.

This page: more recently W.M. use a site. Its objects are the W.M. lifts of special affine opens of X_0, with a 'Zariski topology'. On this site the dagger de Rham complexes Omega^._{A^dagger/W} form a complex of sheaves, and W.M. take its hypercohomology. The results are global invariants that are W-modules. When X_0 is the special fibre of a smooth proper formal scheme X over S = Spf W (the case discussed at the start of the talk), W.M. check (Grothendieck adds '?') that this recovers H^*(X, Omega^._{X/S}). That gives the invariance property (independence of the lift) that Grothendieck had stated earlier.

Section 3, 'Critique of W.M.', begins. Grothendieck praises the construction as an important new idea: it ties the cohomology of varieties in characteristic p to de Rham cohomology in characteristic 0. It yields a cohomology theory that is 'p-adic in char p'. This answers a main criticism of naive de Rham cohomology in char p, whose coefficient ring has characteristic p. The next page completes the sentence: W.M. cohomology has coefficients W(k), whose fraction field K has characteristic 0. Working integrally over W rather than over K gives a notion of p-adic torsion. He then asks whether this is the p-torsion of the p-adic (etale) cohomology of the geometric generic fibre. This motivates the de Rham versus p-adic comparison question, citing Tate's work on H^1 of abelian varieties.

Purpose: to motivate crystalline cohomology as the remedy for W.M.'s defects (dependence on special affines and dagger lifts, results only mod torsion, lack of functoriality and of a site-theoretic foundation).
errors: The complex on the site is written Omega^._{A/k}; it should be the de Rham complex of the weakly complete lift over W (or K), i.e. Omega^._{A^dagger/W}. Most likely a slip of the pen or a transcription issue.

The claim that the global W.M. invariants are W-modules recovering integral H^*(X, Omega^._{X/S}) is hedged by Grothendieck himself ('vérifient (?)'). Integrally, Monsky-Washnitzer cohomology is badly behaved (torsion issues, non-finiteness). The standard statements are after tensoring with K. Indeed the previous page says W.M. prove invariance only mod torsion, so the integral claim here is doubtful as stated.

ideas.what: Global Monsky-Washnitzer cohomology as hypercohomology of the dagger de Rham complex on a site of lifts of special affine opens
ideas.modern_name: Monsky-Washnitzer cohomology (globalized; a precursor of rigid cohomology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Monsky & Washnitzer (1968-1971); globalization later by Berthelot (rigid cohomology), van der Put
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by Coates-Jussila), in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968), introductory survey

ideas.what: Comparison: for X_0 with a smooth proper formal lift X/W, W.M. cohomology equals H^*(X, Omega^._{X/W}), giving independence of the lift
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of Monsky-Washnitzer / rigid cohomology with de Rham cohomology of a lift (Berthelot-Ogus style comparison)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés)

ideas.what: Critique: W.M. gives a p-adic, characteristic-0-coefficient theory in char p, unlike naive de Rham cohomology. Its integral (W-) version gives a candidate notion of p-adic torsion, to be compared with etale torsion of the geometric generic fibre.
ideas.modern_name: Integral p-adic cohomology; torsion comparison of crystalline and etale cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (motivation for crystalline cohomology); torsion comparison by Fontaine-Messing, Faltings, Bhatt-Morrow-Scholze
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes; Récoltes et Semailles (on the 'mysterious functor')

deep.surprise_reason: Expository draft of the Monsky-Washnitzer survey and critique that appears in Grothendieck's published 1968 crystals lectures. It contains no new construction or result. The torsion question on the next page is known historically and was later answered (only an inequality holds in general; see Bhatt-Morrow-Scholze).
transcription_corrections: Line 'met en relation la coh. de var.[?] en car. p[?], avec la cohomologie p-adique[?] / D.R. en car. 0': the sense is 'met en relation la coh. [des variétés] en car. p avec la cohomologie D.R. en car. 0'. The duplicated 'avec la cohomologie p-adique' line is a transcription artefact.

'Elle fournit une théorie hypothétique[?], et "p-adique en car. p", pour / cohomologiques "p-adique en car p", pour / ici W.M.[?] : une des critiques principales' should read approximately: 'Elle fournit une théorie cohomologique "p-adique en car. p", qui évite une des critiques principales qu'on avait faites à D.R. naïve : elle [a comme anneau de coeff. W(k)...]'.
Subscript of Omega on this page: the image looks like Omega^._{A/k} (possibly a dagger on A). Mathematically it should be over W.
The crossed-out word before 'site' (transcribed 'Dagos') is illegible as cancelled; 'Dagger' is a plausible guess.
